The Civil Voaters' Agreement (CVA) is an experiment that anyone may be a part of. It is an entirely voluntary non-binding social contract that, when followed, may benefit the Voat community on the whole.

The agreement is democratically authored, where anyone may propose and vote on changes at regular review periods (likely to be every few months after the initial authorship of the document). The CVA is also "open source", permissively licensed so anyone may fork it and change it however they like, and anyone is free to sign or not sign their name to any version or fork of the agreement they please.

The meat of the Civil Voaters' Agreement is the list of values and habits which, when adopted, probably will make Voat a better community to be a part of. These are things like: browse /v/all/new, don't downvote just because you disagree - downvote if the other person is being a dick though, avoid posting "click-bait" or sensationalized titles, etc.

These things may sound similar to the reddiquette from Reddit, and that is because the basic concept is the same - having a semi-formal list of social mores to help define our culture and values. One key difference is that this document is entirely authored by the community, so if the community no longer believes in something like "don't downvote just because you disagree", it can be changed.

Another important aspect to note is that part of the agreement itself is that signatories don't shame or punish anyone for breaking the agreement after signing, or for removing their signature. This is to solidify the entirely voluntary and non-binding nature of the agreement. We do not want anyone to have the CVA shoved down their throats. From this principle stems an additional directive: do not request or coerce anyone to sign the agreement - a decision to sign should be purely voluntary. It's fine and encouraged to honor signatories and to celebrate the agreement itself though.

I'd like to make clear that this agreement is not officially part of Voat the website/service, it is separate from the Voat User Agreement, and the version of the document that I maintain is not in any way an official or authoritative document in contrast with any forked version which anyone else may maintain. I do not want anyone to feel that I am establishing some sort of dictatorship over it in an unjust manner - I intend on standing by the process and principles I describe for ensuring the document is democratically authored by the community, and providing users the ability to show their support for it through signing their agreement. I'll also do my best to help those interested to be informed about forks and alternative versions of the agreement.

The name is also up for debate if CVA isn't hip enough for casual usage. /v/VoatersAgreement will be used to coordinate reviews and discussions about the agreement. The document itself will be maintained on github. More information to come later.

Wanted to update you and apologize, because i said I'd post about it "tomorrow' two days ago, and i haven't posted anything yet. I've been thinking about how I want to proceed. I've established a rough roadmap/timeline which i think will work.

Tentative plan is this: very soon, as soon as I have a draft ready that I'm comfortable with, I'll publish it as version 0.1 of my branch of the agreement. I'll solicit input from people, and edit it on my own in vaguely democratic process, but mostly with editorial discretion. The result of this will be a v. 0.5 or something document that will serve as a beta test for about a month or two, where anyone may sign their agreement with the principles it describes.

During that time, anyone may make a pull request with any changes they wish to see. After the beta-test period is up, I'll attempt to facilitate the first formal convention for the democratic editorship of the civil voaters' agreement. I'm picturing a two-week process. First week, people can vote and continue to make additional pull requests. Second week, no new pull requests will be considered for this round, but any changes proposed up until that point are still able to be voted on. At the conclusion of the two weeks, the winning changes will be merged and the version of the document updated to 1.0, it will be given a mnemonic codename and published officially. Anyone may then sign this version if they wish, or not. People can just stick to the beta version, or whatever. completely voluntary. Depending on how things go, I'm imagining formal revision/amendment conventions like that every three months maybe... maybe longer.

This is all just tentative plans, subject to change. The way I'm viewing this is that there are three concepts at play: the idea of a Voaters' Agreement, my specific version of the voaters' agreement, and the democratic process I'll be attempting to facilitate for revision of my specific version of the voaters' agreement.

Hi! I am very optimistic about what the voat community could potentially evolve into. My final straw with reddit was when I saw a blatant repost of a picture that had been on the internet for ages, in which OP claimed he had taken this picture with his mother, so I simply said "No you didn't" and promptly received 30 or so downvotes. I see so much of the same content or content that just sucks in general. I think it will be interesting to see how some of the actual quality subreddits will migrate over to voat and what that process will look like.

I have one question though: what should voat learn from the mistakes of reddit and how will they be solved?

I remember once I was on the Cube World subreddit on a post about how the creator of the game hadn't released an update for ages. I made a comment saying how I think we need to give them some consideration since it is only him and his wife working on the game. And you know what I got? You guessed it, downvotes. That sort of thing doesn't happen here, I'm sure you will enjoy your time here.

As for your question, I think we need to remember our past, but not dwell on it. Atko has already implemented securities to prevent vote brigades, such as the 100 CCP minimum required to downvote, and only allowing one vote on a submission per IP to prevent people making multiple accounts. I think in the years to come we may have challenges to overcome, but we wont worry about that till they get here.

Anyway, welcome to Voat! If you have any questions about the site feel free to ask, I'm happy to answer.

The main thing Voat should take away from Reddit is not to ban people or remove comments without laid out reasons why it was done.
